observations: VoiceOutputPacket permits commit_eligible only when playback_state is completed and heard_fraction is exactly 1.0.
advance_output derives commit_eligible only from completed plus heard_fraction 1.0.
barge-in/interruption transitions outstanding output to an interrupted/cancelled terminal state with commit_eligible false while retaining heard_fraction as playback evidence.
session close rejects result_ref/result_sha256 when there is no fully-heard commit-eligible output; only commit-eligible packets receive a VoiceOutcome reference.
current_f2_contract_evidence.interpretation: The current deterministic F2 voice contract treats a partially heard interrupted assistant response as non-commit-eligible as a whole. Heard fraction is retained as evidence/measurement, not as proof that a partial assistant semantic prefix must become committed conversational truth.

observed_behavior_from_existing_t7_evide: conversation.item.truncate is recognized but deliberately performs no additional server-state mutation.
cancelled/failed/incomplete response handling rolls back provisional assistant/tool generation.

pinned upstream unit tests show rollback removes eager provisional assistant/tool items, rejects late writes for the cancelled generation, preserves previously committed user history and excludes cancelled content from compaction.

reconciliation.prior_apparent_conflict: One Trigger-7 delta treated exact heard-prefix persistence as a potential compatibility requirement, while later pinned-source/unit-test evidence showed whole-response rollback after cancellation.
reconciliation.resolution: Under the current F2 commit contract, whole-response rollback is not itself a prefix-amnesia product failure because interrupted output is non-commit-eligible. Exact heard-boundary data remains important for playback stopping, diagnostics, latency and preventing unheard/stale producer leakage, but it is not presently an authority rule that a heard semantic prefix from an interrupted response must be committed into the next conversational model context.

must_fail_if: any assistant text/audio/tool/effect semantics from a cancelled non-commit-eligible response regain authoritative next-turn influence
a late cancelled-generation tool result or output chunk regains ownership
client playback continues beyond the measured cancellation/heard boundary contrary to the F2 playback state
duplicate/stale cancellation or truncate corrupts a newer turn
runtime_oracle_refinement.must_not_fail_merely_if: The raw HF server drops the entire provisional interrupted response, including content heard before barge-in, provided F2 keeps that response non-commit-eligible and no separate current F2 contract requires partial-prefix semantic persistence.
runtime_oracle_refinement.reopen_prefix_persistence_if: A newer canonical F2 contract explicitly promotes partially heard interrupted output into committed conversational state or model-context authority.

next_exact_action: Do not open another Trigger-7 architecture lane or duplicate runtime dispatch. Trigger4 should execute the already-routed HF cancellation/runtime packet on the pinned speech-to-speech subject in the admitted VPS sandbox, using the refined F2 oracle: interrupted response remains wholly non-commit-eligible; prove no cancelled assistant/tool semantics regain next-turn authority, prove playback stops at the measured boundary, and preserve exact late/stale-race evidence. Promote only executed scope.
